title: Per-Run Mini Matrix (Latency & Cost quicksheet)
content:
Purpose: tiny per-run cheat sheet I keep on my laptop to compare single-run throughput vs batch tradeoffs. Use for quick callouts in standups and to decide which experiments to promote to official bench.

Table (CSV-style):
run_id, date, model, quant, batch_size, prefix_cache, avg_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_second, est_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd, notes
r-2025-06-12-01, 2025-06-12, orca-mini-7b, fp16, 1, no, 42.3, 89.1, 120.4, 0.062, baseline single-token latency
r-2025-06-12-02, 2025-06-12, orca-mini-7b, q4_0, 1, no, 35.7, 72.6, 142.6, 0.048, q4_0 wins latency & cost
r-2025-06-15-03, 2025-06-15, orca-mini-7b, q4_0, 4, no, 80.2, 150.9, 268.0, 0.033, batching improves T/S but p95 still high
r-2025-06-18-04, 2025-06-18, orca-mini-7b, q4_0, 8, yes(prefix), 125.8, 190.4, 410.2, 0.025, prefix cache reduces compute; good for chat-like flows
r-2025-06-20-05, 2025-06-20, llama2-13b, fp16, 1, no, 210.5, 420.7, 80.1, 0.18, heavier model; unsuitable for low-latency routes
r-2025-06-24-06, 2025-06-24, orca-mini-7b, q2_k, 1, no, 48.9, 95.0, 110.0, 0.035, q2_k artifacting on long tokens (see notes)

Quick calcs / heuristics I eyeball:
- tokens_per_second ≈ (batch_size * avg_generation_tokens) / avg_latency_seconds — I normalize generation tokens to 15 for chat prompt tests unless otherwise noted
- est_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd: used internal unit cost macro (back-of-envelope); q4_0 = ~0.78x fp16 cost for this runtime

Observations (rough):
- q4_0 on orca-mini gives best latency/cost tradeoff for short-turn chat (1-4 toks). If p95 is acceptable (<180ms) it should be candidate for hosted low-tier SKU.
- batching (4-8) jumps throughput substantially but increases tail latency; prefix cache recovers p95 for repeated contexts.
- llama2-13b is still too costly for low-latency interactive paths; keep for higher-quality generation routes only.
- q2_k shows weird dropouts on long suffixes after ~640 tokens — probably quantization instability; flag for applied-ml to repro with targeted eval set (ticket linked).

TODO / next runs:
- run r-2025-07-03-07: orca-mini-7b q4_0 batch=2 prefix=yes, measure p99 and p50, add jitter/CPU load test
- run r-2025-07-03-08: orca-mini-7b q2_k batch=1 prefix=no, regenerate with extended prompt (1200t) to stress long-run artifact
- run r-2025-07-10-09: llama2-13b q4_0 single token latency with KV cache priming (compare to fp16 baseline)

Notes-to-self:
- When presenting numbers, always include sequence length used and how tokens_per_second was computed; reviewers ask for it every time.
- Pull in cost macros from billing repo before sending to product team (link above). My est values are fine for relative ranking but not for quotes.
- Keep a separate column for 'prompt_len' next time; current table conflates generation-only metrics.

Scratch math examples (hand):
- convert avg_latency_ms -> tokens_per_second: if avg_latency_ms=42.3 and gen tokens=15 => 15 / (42.3/1000) ≈ 354 t/s for batch=1? (my table uses lower T/S because measured includes overhead; re-check measurement script)

Slack refs:
- related convo: #serve-runtime → thread: "q4_0 tail improvements" (2025-06-18) — saved some tips from Rafael about kernel select order

End of sheet. Reuse this as quick lookup during triage and for standup highlights. Keep it tiny; port winners to /shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/benchmarks when stable.
